paper.title: Dynamic Cheatsheet: Test-Time Learning with Adaptive Memory

assessment.evidence_level_note: Memory written from earlier test items is read on later ones, and DC-∅ (same structured prompt, empty memory) isolates its effect (e.g. Claude AIME 2024 36.7→50.0, GPT-4o Game of 24 19→99). Construction stream = evaluation stream (prequential, label-free); no frozen-memory or held-out evaluation, so not improver/transfer.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Author-reported, single run, one ordering: on Claude 3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4o a label-free, self-curated text memory raises accuracy over the same-prompt empty-memory control on AIME, GPQA (Claude), Game of 24 (GPT-4o) and Math Equation Balancer, with largest gains where a reusable code routine exists; no or negative gain for GPT-4o on knowledge tasks and for smaller models. The abstract's 'more than doubled' is against the minimal-prompt BL. Not reproduced.
unresolved: Order/seed variance (single run; order said to matter, opus:O07).
Curator vs alternative abstraction/editing scheme under equal budget.
Three prose-vs-table number mismatches (son55:E018, opus:O01, opus:O03); Table values used.

G.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. The fixed object (static retrieval corpus / raw history; no cross-query curation) is named, but the closest memory neighbours (Buffer-of-Thoughts, Thought-Retriever, MemPrompt, Reflexion) are distinguished only in related-work prose, and 'no weight updates' carries much of the framing.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. Generation/curation split and the DC-Cu vs DC-RS ordering are explicit and make checkable predictions against DC-∅, DR and FH (curated > raw retrieval/history > empty), plus the capacity dependence that is observed. The self-judged write gate (opus:O05) is the weak assumption.

X.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Write/refine/delete/merge are left to the curator prompt and the whole memory is rewritten each step (truncation observed by the authors); no external gate, versioning, rollback or conflict rule.

E.measurement.reason: Opus sides with son55. Ground-truth answers make the underlying verifiers credible, but the 'Functionally Correct' checker used for AIME/Game of 24/Balancer is undefined beyond 'flexible' (opus:O04), and the prose contradicts the tables three times: GPQA GPT-4o DC-RS 58.1 vs Table 1 57.1 (son55:E018 vs son55:E013), GPT-4o FH 'fell to 6.7%' vs Table 2 13.3 (opus:O01/O02, found by sol), and GPT-4o-mini '20.0% boost' for +3.3 points (opus:O03). sol's 3 counted only one mismatch.

E.causality.reason: Opus sides with son55. The store-off control keeps the identical structured prompt (DC-∅), retrieval-without-curation (DR) is run on every task, uncurated full history (FH) on AIME, and a 3-sample MV over DC-∅ partly controls extra compute (opus:O08); together these rule out the prompt and simple retrieval explanations for the main gains. Not 4: no budget-matched alternative curator, DR ≈ DC on some cells (Claude AIME 2020–24 39.1 vs 38.4/40.6), FH only on AIME. sol's 2 under-credits these controls.

E.holdout.reason: Shared-error correction (both seats 2). Memory is built from the evaluated stream itself (prequential; no labels, opus:O05), with no frozen-memory or independent held-out evaluation, no contamination check on AIME/GPQA, k chosen on an unspecified set (opus:O06), one ordering whose effect the authors acknowledge (opus:O07), and cross-model memory transfer reported only as 'mixed'.
